Flood Insurance in Myrtle Beach: When Your Mortgage Requires It

Buying on the Grand Strand? Here's when your lender needs flood insurance, how to check the map, and the local discounts most buyers don't know about.

Paul Hankins
Founder & Broker · NMLS #281393

If you're buying in Myrtle Beach or anywhere on the Grand Strand, your lender will require flood insurance when the home sits in a high-risk flood zone. That's any FEMA zone starting with A or V. The rule covers almost every home loan: conventional, FHA, VA and bank loans. It also applies in a few protected coastal barrier areas. Outside those areas, flood insurance is usually your choice.

Myrtle Beach flood zone map: how to look up a house

Type the address into FEMA's flood map. Horry County also posts its FEMA flood maps on the county site. The maps in effect for Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Conway and the rest of Horry County date from December 16, 2021. In Georgetown County, the Town of Pawleys Island's map dates from May 9, 2023. The map for the rest of the county, outside the City of Georgetown, dates from June 18, 2025.

Here is what the letters mean:

ZoneWhat it meansRequired for your loan?
Starts with A (like AE)High risk.Yes
Starts with V (like VE)High risk on the oceanfront, where waves add to the flooding.Yes
XModerate or low risk.No, but you can still buy it

Once you're under contract and apply, the lender orders an official flood zone check on the home. If it's in a high-risk zone, you'll get a written notice before closing. A shed, or a detached garage with no living space, in the zone doesn't trigger the rule when the house itself is outside it.

Some Grand Strand communities get a discount on flood insurance

Here's a local detail that can save you money. Several Grand Strand communities take extra flood-safety steps through FEMA's Community Rating System, and in return federal flood policies there cost less. The discount depends on where the home is:

CommunityHigh-risk zone discountOther zones
City of Myrtle Beach25%10%
Unincorporated Horry County (like Carolina Forest, Socastee and Garden City)25%10%
Town of Pawleys Island25%10%
City of North Myrtle Beach20%10%
Town of Surfside Beach15%5%
Unincorporated Georgetown County (like Murrells Inlet) and the City of Georgetown15%5%
Conway, Loris, Aynor, Atlantic Beach, Briarcliffe AcresNoneNone

These discounts apply to policies through FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program, and they follow town limits, not mailing addresses. Ask your insurance agent to confirm it's on your quote.

Is flood insurance required in Zone X?

Usually not. Your lender won't require it in Zone X. But Zone X isn't "no risk", and homes there do flood. Most homeowners insurance doesn't cover flooding, so you need a separate flood policy to be covered. In the City of Myrtle Beach, a federal flood policy on a Zone X home also gets the 10% discount above.

How much flood insurance does the lender require?

The lender needs coverage on the building equal to the lowest of these three amounts:

  • what it would cost to rebuild the house;
  • $250,000, the most a standard federal flood policy covers on a house;
  • your loan amount.

Coverage for your furniture and belongings is usually your choice. The required coverage is on the house, not the land under it.

How much is flood insurance in Myrtle Beach?

There's no one number. Federal flood policies are priced home by home, based on how high the house sits, how close it is to water and what it would cost to rebuild. Two houses on the same street can have very different bills. Get a quote on the house you want before you make an offer.

The premium then becomes part of your monthly housing cost, just like taxes and homeowners insurance. Lenders compare that total with your income, so a high flood premium can lower the price you qualify for.

An example. Two Horry County houses have the same price. One is in Zone X. The other sits in an AE zone near the marsh. The AE house needs a flood policy, and that premium is added to the monthly cost. With the same income, the buyer qualifies for a little less on the AE house.

A few more things to know:

  • It's usually paid through escrow. Regulated lenders generally collect the premium with your monthly payment.
  • No waiting period when you buy. A federal flood policy bought with your new loan starts at closing, as long as you apply and pay by closing. Without a loan, a new policy normally waits 30 days.
  • Private flood insurance works too. Lenders accept private policies that give at least the same coverage as a federal policy.
  • Wind is a separate question. In Horry County, homes east of U.S. 17 or Bypass 17, whichever is farther west, are in South Carolina's coastal wind pool area. In Myrtle Beach, that line is the Bypass. That affects the wind part of your homeowners insurance, not flood.

Can a house be taken out of a flood zone?

Sometimes. If the ground right next to the house is higher than the flood level on the map, the owner can ask FEMA for a Letter of Map Amendment, called a LOMA. If FEMA agrees, the lender no longer requires flood insurance on that house. If the home you're buying already has one, ask the seller for a copy.

Buying a condo in a flood zone?

For an oceanfront or marsh-side condo in a high-risk zone, the lender looks for a master flood policy the HOA carries on the building. If the HOA's coverage for your unit falls short of what your loan needs, you buy a policy of your own to fill the gap. More in our guide to Myrtle Beach condo financing.

Flood insurance questions

Do I need flood insurance in Myrtle Beach?

Only if the home is in a high-risk FEMA flood zone, one starting with A or V, or in a protected coastal barrier area. Then your lender requires it. In Zone X it's your choice, though homes there can still flood.

Is flood insurance cheaper in Myrtle Beach?

Federal flood policies in the City of Myrtle Beach get a 25% discount in high-risk zones and 10% elsewhere, through FEMA's Community Rating System. The City of North Myrtle Beach gets 20% and 10%, and the Town of Surfside Beach 15% and 5%.

Is flood insurance required to be escrowed?

Usually. Federally regulated lenders must collect flood premiums through escrow, with a few exceptions, so the premium is paid along with your monthly mortgage payment.

Is there a waiting period for flood insurance when buying a house?

No. A federal flood policy bought with a new loan takes effect at closing, as long as you apply and pay by then. Without a loan, a new policy normally starts 30 days after you apply and pay.
